newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - CARTEL DEMISE TO DULL PPC YR SHR.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - CARTEL DEMISE TO DULL PPC YR SHR.

text.p: Pretoria Portland Cement would post flat results for the year to September 30 amid low cement and lime sales and hefty costs associated with the demise of the cement cartel, analysts said on Friday.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings rising around five percent to between 477.0 and 500.0 cents with consensus at 489.7 cents. The dividend was expected to rise to 300 cents from 285 cents before.
"Their results will come out flat on low cement and lime volumes," said Johan Snyman, an analyst at brokerage ING Barings.
"They also had to prepare for the post cartel environment and had to invest in information technology, transport and administration...The end result is fairly flat," Snyman said.
Another analyst said: "I expect their profit will be negative before tax. (However) a write-back of Secondary Tax on Companies will boost them."
The cartel which dominated South Africa's cement industry for 25 years was dismantled on September 30 this year.

Under the cartel prices were fixed and all distribution was done by a single company, Cement Distributors of South Africa Ltd, which was jointly owned by the country's three largest industry players -- PPC, Alpha Ltd and Blue Circle, a Murray and Roberts Holdings Ltd subsidiary.
Analysts said in the long term PPC was better placed than its competitors to compete in a deregulated environment.
"Preparations for the demise of the cartel cost them. But they will be the best after it," an analyst said.
